chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from one of his companions, mentioning from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Huzayfa ibn Mansur, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'A group of people had little politeness towards the people, so they were expelled from Quraysh, and I swear by Allah, there was no problem with their lineage, and a group from other than Quraysh had good politeness, so they were joined with the elevated household.'
He said, 'Then he said: The one who restrains his hand from the people, rather, he restrains one hand from them but they restrain many hands from him.'

key_terms.الْبَيْتُ الرَّفِيع: The elevated household, referring to high status or the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.قُرَيْش: The tribe of Quraysh, often used to denote noble lineage or elite status
key_terms.مُدَارَاة: Politeness, social grace, or tact in dealing with others

ai.seo_question: How does politeness affect social standing and reciprocity according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the principle of *modararah* (social tact and courtesy) as a decisive factor for communal acceptance, superseding tribal lineage (*hasab*) as evidenced by the Quraysh's rejection of the tactless despite their nobility. The Imam further elucidates the reciprocal nature of social interaction, warning that withholding one's hand in generosity or kindness isolates the individual, whereas restraint in conflict or generosity invites reciprocal treatment from the community. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) as a practical manifestation of faith in daily social dynamics.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from one of his companions, mentioning from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Huzeyfa Bin Mansour who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘A group of people with little politeness towards the people, so they were expelled from the Qureysh, and I swear by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, there was no problem with their lineage, and a group from other than the Qureysh, their politeness was good, so they were joined with the elevated households’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who restrains a hand from the people (not helping them), so rather, one hand would be restrained from them but lots of hands would be restrained from him’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from certain individuals of his people whom he has mentioned (in his book) from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Hudhayfa ibn Mansur who has said the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) say, ‘Certain people lacked gentle dealings with others, they were expelled from the tribe of Quraysh. I swear by Allah, there was nothing wrong with their birth. On the other hand, certain people who were not from the tribe of Quraysh dealt with people gently and they were joined in the family of superior status.’
The Imam then said, ‘One who holds his hand back from people he only holds back one hand but they (people) hold back from him many hands.’”
